description: A TCT whose signature does not validate under the resolved issuer key MUST be rejected with TCT_SIGNATURE_INVALID before any remote revocation lookup is attempted. Verifiers that route revocation lookups (HTTPS fetch of `ListRevoked`, DNS resolution of the issuing peer's endpoint, or cache writes keyed off `tct.issuer` / `tct.jti`) before signature verification are vulnerable to network-amplification DoS, revocation-cache pollution, and telemetry manipulation against arbitrary AIDs — `tct.issuer` and `tct.jti` are attacker-controlled bytes until the TCT signature is verified. This fixture pins the ordering requirement in RFC-AITP-0008 §3.3: the conformance harness instruments the revocation source and asserts it was NOT called when the TCT signature is invalid. A purely local, side-effect-free in-memory deny-list check that performs no network I/O and no cache writes derived from issuer-provided input is exempt from this ordering requirement (RFC-AITP-0008 §3.3) and MAY run before signature verification.

expected.rationale: Signature is invalid; the revocation source MUST NOT be consulted. Asserting the instrumented revocation lookup was not called pins the ordering requirement in RFC-AITP-0008 §3.3 — without this side-effect check, a verifier that runs revocation lookup before signature verification can pass `error_code: TCT_SIGNATURE_INVALID` while still having performed the attacker-triggered network fetch.
